chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Abbas, from Abdullah al-Kahili, from Abu al-Faraj, who said:
I performed tawaf with Abu Abdillah عليه السلام for five circuits. Then I said: I wish to visit a sick person. So he said: Mark your place, then go and visit him, then return and complete your tawaf.

So this does not contradict the earlier reports, because completion was only permitted for him since he had performed more than half. Repetition is required when what was done was less than half. No one may say: Why did you not also interpret the two reports as permitting completion in the tawaf of supererogatory worship, while requiring repetition in the tawaf of an obligatory act in every case? Because if that were so, there would be no difference between when it was more than half and when it was less than that, whereas they عليهم السلام did distinguish between the two tawafs when it was less than half and when it was more than that. This indicates that when it exceeds half, there is no difference between them regarding the permissibility of building upon it, except insofar as it is tawaf of an obligation, for the tawaf of supererogatory worship may be built upon in every case. Moreover, reports have also been transmitted mentioning the tawaf of obligation and that it is permissible to build upon it, so it is not possible to interpret them according to this view. He narrated that.

key_terms.أَتِمَّ: complete; finish the remaining portion of the act
key_terms.النِّصْفِ: half; the midpoint used as the legal threshold in the ruling
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition; restarting the act from the beginning
key_terms.الْبِنَاءِ: building upon; continuing from what has already been completed
key_terms.طُفْتُ: I performed tawaf; refers to circumambulating the Ka'bah
key_terms.مَرِيضًا: a sick person; the person being visited

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on interrupting tawaf for an excuse before completing seven circuits?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of interrupting tawaf due to an excuse, such as visiting a sick person. It indicates that if more than half of the tawaf has been completed, one may return and complete it, whereas if less than half has been completed, it must be repeated; it also discusses the distinction between obligatory and supererogatory tawaf.
